name: Trigger-Marker Race-Surface Mitigation (Inflection Gold Pipeline)
description: Eliminate the silent-failure surfaces in the Inflection gold-chain trigger contract between `inf-gold-trigger` Lambda and `inf-gold-layer-runner` EC2. Three structurally distinct hardening levers: (A) install `inf-gold-dispatcher.service` systemd daemon on EC2 to close race surface #2 (Lambda's pending-marker pattern when EC2 hot has no consumer; silent no-op); (B) Lambda pre-write `chain_in_flight` check + stale-marker reject to close race surface #1 (preemptive boot consumes stale marker; wrong-mode fire); (C) accurate `source` provenance in mode-marker JSON (currently inherits Lambda env-var default `"cron"` regardless of invocation path). Empirically anchored on 3 same-day incidents 2026-05-14: incident #1 stale-marker race (chain_full_20260514_141419 wrong-mode kill+re-dispatch 49min recovery), incident #3 hot-state silent no-op (18:14:06Z Lambda invoke → ~13min elapsed → SSM-direct workaround required at 18:20:52Z). Race surface #1 + #2 together prove the trigger flow is fragile in BOTH boot-state directions. DS~D-attributed memory entry `feedback_lambda_pending_marker_no_daemon.md` banked 2026-05-14 18:30Z with empirical contrast pair (Lambda hot no-op vs SSM-direct clean). Sister to ADHC_COMPIL_V4.030 `comp-pipescript stale-marker` compiler-side companion (already authored + held by COO in v0.5 batch).
